nodes.characterization_summary: Raman peaks of Fe2O3 at 221 cm⁻¹ (A1g(1)), 243 cm⁻¹ (Eg(1)), 288 cm⁻¹ (Eg(2)), 405 cm⁻¹ (Eg(4)), 500 cm⁻¹ (A1g(2)), 608 cm⁻¹ (Eg(5)), and 660 cm⁻¹ (Eu) confirm Fe2O3 formation; FeCrO3 shows slightly blue-shifted peaks with increased Eu half-peak width indicating Cr incorporation and stronger Fe-O bond.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The peaks recorded on the control Fe oxides at 221 cm⁻¹ (A1g(1)), 243 cm⁻¹ (Eg(1)), 288 cm⁻¹ (Eg(2)), 405 cm⁻¹ (Eg(4)), 500 cm⁻¹ (A1g(2)), 608 cm⁻¹ (Eg(5)), and 660 cm⁻¹ (Eu) are attributed to the characteristic vibrations of Fe2O3 ... Those Raman peaks of Fe-Cr oxides are slightly blue-shifted relative to Fe2O3, and the half-peak width of Eu increases, indicating that successful incorporation of Cr into Fe2O3 improves the strength of the Fe-O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe-O bond distance shrinks from 1.43 Å in Fe2O3 to 1.41 Å in FeCrO3; Cr-O bond distance shrinks from 1.45 Å in Cr2O3 to 1.41 Å in FeCrO3, indicating more compact lattice by regular Cr doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis also reveals similar results ... The Fe-O bond distance shrinks from 1.43Å in Fe2O3 to 1.41Å in Fe-Cr oxides, and the Cr-O bond distance shrinks from 1.45Å in Cr2O3 to 1.41Å in Fe-Cr oxides, suggesting that a more compact lattice is achieved by regular Cr doping.

nodes.characterization_summary: (104) crystal plane spacing in FeCrO3 is 0.268 nm vs 0.270 nm in Fe2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) image further confirms the above conclusions. Compared to Fe2O3 (0.270 nm, Figure S6), the (104) crystal plane spacing in Fe-Cr oxides is slightly smaller at 0.268 nm (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe/Cr atomic ratio ~1:1 in FeCrO3; Fe 2p peaks shift from 711.5 eV (2p3/2) and 725.0 eV (2p1/2) in Fe2O3 to 711.1 eV and 724.6 eV; Cr 2p shift to higher binding energies 576.8 eV (2p3/2) and 586.5 eV (2p1/2); Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ ratio increases from 0.7 (Fe2O3) to 2.15 (FeCrO3).
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) results show that the atomic ratio of Fe and Cr in the Fe-Cr oxide is about 1:1 (Figure S7) ... The Fe 2p peaks of FeCrO3 shift from 711.5 eV (2p3/2) and 725.0 eV (2p1/2) in Fe2O3 to lower binding energies of 711.1 eV (2p3/2) and 724.6 eV (2p1/2) ... When Cr is homogeneously doped into Fe2O3, the ratios of Fe²⁺/Fe³⁺ increases from 0.7 (Fe2O3) to 2.15 (FeCrO3), confirming that less electronegative Cr is beneficial to stabilize less positively charged Fe²⁺.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCrO3 diffraction patterns match PDF#02-1357; Fe2O3 matches PDF#33-0664.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The assignment of an equivalent amount of Fe to be replaced by Cr is further confirmed by X-ray diffraction (XRD) spectroscopy ... The diffraction patterns of Fe-Cr oxides show a perfect match with those of FeCrO3 (PDF#02-1357), while the control Fe oxide is indexed to Fe2O3 (PDF#33-0664).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCrO3 shows Cr atoms arranged in alternating cation layers with Fe atoms; bright spots = Fe, dark spots = Cr atomic columns.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cr atoms were observed to be arranged in alternative cation layers with Fe atoms in the lattice of FeCrO3, while only Fe were observed as cations in the lattice of Fe2O3 ... The bright spots in the images correspond to Fe atomic columns, which show a distinct contrast to the darker Cr atomic columns.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe, Cr, and O atoms uniformly distributed across FeCrO3 nanosheet; Fe/Cr atomic ratio ~1:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Supportively, elemental mapping images show that Fe, Cr, and O atoms are uniformly distributed across the nanosheet of FeCrO3 ... X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) results show that the atomic ratio of Fe and Cr in the Fe-Cr oxide is about 1:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe oxidation state in FeCrO3 is +2.67 vs +2.96 in Fe2O3.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A similar conclusion can also be drawn from X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) measurements ... The oxidation state of Fe in FeCrO3 is projected to be +2.67 by K-edge energy analysis, making reference to Fe foil and commercial Fe2O3 ... This value is lower than that of Fe2O3 (+2.96).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe2O3 and FeCrO3 display hexagonal nanosheet morphology with diagonal length of 155 nm and thickness of 20 nm (20 nanosheets counted); Cr impregnation causes no notable morphology changes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show that as-synthesized Fe-Cr oxides display a hexagonal nanosheet morphology similar to that of Fe oxide, with a typical diagonal length of 155 nm and a thickness of 20 nm (20 nanosheets counted).
